summary: The root وَطَرٌ (watar) refers to a want, need, or an object one desires to accomplish. It's often used in the phrase "قَضَيْتُ وَطَرِى" meaning "I accomplished my want.
lane: وَطَرٌ ذ A want; an object of want or need: (Zj, S, A, Msb, K:) or one which one purposes to accomplish: (Lth:) or for which one is anxious, (A, K,) or desirous: (Msb:) pl. أَوْطَارٌ . (S, A, Msb, K.) It has no verb. (Kh, S, Msb.) You say, قَضَيْتُ وَطَرِى I accomplished, or obtained, my want, &c. (A, Msb, K.) And قَضَيْتُ مِنْ كَذَا وَطَرِى I accomplished my want of such a thing [so as to have no further need of it: see Kur, xxxiii. 37, in two places]. (Lth.)
